shadows.value: coral #FF8A65 at 40% alpha, radius 13% of dial radius, blur 4% of dial radius

motion.name: native-controls

dialGeometry.box: 280pt square; ring of about 240pt with day-part labels outside it
dialGeometry.arcs: radius 66% of r, stroke 2.2% of r, primary at 45% alpha, 0.035 rad gap at each end
dialGeometry.dots: radius 76% of r; size min(2.2% of r, 22% of pitch); on the hour x1.45, capped at 34% of pitch
dialGeometry.muted: dots drawn as rings, primary at 80% alpha, stroke half the dot size
dialGeometry.labels: near edge at 84% of r, pushed out by half the label's extent along the radius
dialGeometry.now: coral dot 5% of r inside a band-coloured ring of 6.5% of r
dialGeometry.centre: time (display, fitted) over next announcement (body, 1.3), inset 64pt

decisions.what: Dot Dial on Clear Sky replaces the Alpona Dial world
decisions.why: The user chose logo C and theme 2, each from four options on a variants page; the earth palette read too dark.
V-shaped hands read as a tick mark at small sizes.

decisions.what: App icons at 32px and below and the 1x menu-bar template keep only the four quarter-hour dots
decisions.why: The eight small dots blur away at those sizes.
Day-part labels sit outside a ring of about 240pt and need that room at the 480pt window width.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Dot Dial on Clear Sky"**

The day is a dial of dots on a clear morning sky. The settings window opens on a pale sky band holding today as a 24-hour ring, noon at the top and midnight at the bottom, with one blue fingertip dot for every announcement the clock will make and a coral dot for now. The day is drawn, not listed. Below the band the window turns quiet and native: an airy blue-white ground, white outlined cards, macOS controls tinted sky blue. The dial is the one loud thing; everything under it stays out of its way.

Density is low and type is large, because the users include elders and low-vision people. Every row uses the same generous 16pt and is ranked by weight. Bangla leads and English follows, both set in Hind Siliguri, so switching language never changes the voice of the page.

The logo is the same dial idea reduced to a clock: twelve dots, the four quarter hours larger, the twelve in coral, two round-capped hands at ten o'clock. It was chosen by the user from four logos (logo C) together with this theme (theme 2 of four), replacing the earlier Alpona Dial world, which read too dark and earthy. One painter draws the logo in the app, the app icon and the menu-bar template, so the icons can never drift from the logo.
keyCharacteristics: A pale sky band holding a 280pt day dial, and nothing else.
Sky blue for the dial, the logo and every control; coral only for now and the logo's twelve.
Ink, not white, for every word on the band.
Fingertip dots are the only ornament: twelve on the logo, one per announcement on the dial.
One row size (16pt), ranked by weight.
Native macOS control forms (Cupertino switch, slider, sliding segmented control, radio, pop-up button).
Flat chrome: depth comes from hairline borders and tonal grounds, not shadows.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Sky blue is the only colour a control, a dot or a hand may take. Section titles use a deeper blue; nothing else competes.

rules.name: The One Coral Rule
rules.body: Coral marks now, and the twelve on the logo. It never fills a control, never sets text and never decorates.

rules.name: The Ink On Sky Rule
rules.body: The band is pale and its words are ink. Blue is for what is drawn on it (arcs, dots), ink for what is read on it (time, day parts, next announcement).

rules.name: The One Row Size Rule
rules.body: Every row is 16pt. Rank comes from weight (700 section, 500 title, 400 subtitle) and colour, never from shrinking text. Nothing a user reads in the settings goes below 14pt.

rules.name: The Flat Chrome Rule
rules.body: Settings surfaces never take a custom shadow. Depth is tonal: ground, card, track, thumb.

rules.name: The Clock First Rule
rules.body: The logo must read as a clock before anything else. The hands show 10:00, not 10:08: V-shaped hands read as a tick mark at small sizes.

rules.name: The Quarter Dots Rule
rules.body: At 32px and below, and in the 1x menu-bar template, the logo keeps only the four quarter-hour dots.

dos: **Do** draw every brand mark from the dot-dial painter, choosing its variant by size: full colour above 64px, 1.25x weight at 64px and below, quarter dots only at 32px and below, template at 1.2x in the 2x menu bar and 1.45x with quarter dots only at 1x.
**Do** keep the logo's hands at 10:00, minute hand to twelve, hour hand to ten.
**Do** keep every settings row at 16pt and rank by weight: 700 for section titles, 500 for row titles, 400 for subtitles.
**Do** tint every control sky blue (#2F74D0 light, #8AB8F5 dark) and use native macOS forms: Cupertino switch, adaptive slider, sliding segmented control, Cupertino radio, pop-up button.
**Do** set every word on the band in ink, and draw only arcs and dots in blue.
**Do** make every dial dot a real announcement; muted turns dots to outlines, quiet hours leave the ring bare.
**Do** open secondary content such as credits as a pushed page with a back button.
donts: **Don't** put a list, a clock-face icon or any second element in the header band; the dial owns it.
**Don't** use coral for anything but now and the logo's twelve, or any colour but sky blue for a control.
**Don't** give the logo V-shaped hands (such as 10:08); at small sizes they read as a tick mark.
**Don't** add ornament to the settings chrome; dots are the only ornament, and they live in the dial and the logo.
**Don't** give cards or controls custom shadows; separate them with hairlines and tone.
**Don't** shrink text to create hierarchy, or set any settings text below 14pt.
**Don't** use Material's underlined dropdowns or filled segmented buttons where a macOS form exists.
**Don't** open credits in a modal dialog.

decisions: Past announcements on the dial are dimmed to 35% so upcoming ones stand out.
The coral now dot has a #C7471F edge ring so it holds 3:1 against the #E1EEFD band.
Tiny logo sizes (32px and below, 1x template) use a 42% minute hand and a 44% hour hand: a gap below the twelve dot, and an hour hand that survives as a hand.
